clue.text: Apple perhaps offered by snake before the lapse of Adam and Eve

indicators.note: before places the snake word ahead of the lapse word in the answer

parts.note: to snake is to wind, as a path or river twists along

parts.words: the lapse of Adam and Eve
parts.note: the Fall is the biblical lapse of Adam and Eve in Eden

explanation.surface: The serpent in Eden tempts Eve with an apple just before the first humans sin.
explanation.walkthrough: The Eden picture makes 'Apple' look literal, but here it is only an example of fruit blown off a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit blown down from a tree by the wind is called by this name, and an apple is a typical instance.

clue.text: What I could keep, eliminating team's openers

definitions.text: What I could keep, eliminating team's openers

parts.words: What I could keep, eliminating team's openers
parts.note: in cricket a keeper keeps this, and taking one dismisses the opening batsmen of the batting side

explanation.surface: Someone muses on what they might hold onto while getting rid of a side's first players.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket: the 'keeper' (wicketkeeper) stands behind the stumps, and each dismissal of a batsman, such as the openers who bat first, is also called by this word.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the stumps a keeper guards, and also a dismissal of a batsman, share this name.

clue.text: Light rain comes from this

definitions.meaning: a halo of light round a saint's head

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a halo round a holy figure's head and a low grey rain cloud.

clue.text: Unaffected by heat, even though upset over censure

indicators.note: in a down clue over puts the first piece above, so ahead of, the next
in a down clue upset turns the word for even though upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: if can mean even though, as in 'pleasant if dull'
a reproof is a rebuke or censure

explanation.surface: Something stays unaffected by heat even though someone is upset about being criticised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns IF into FI, which sits 'over' (before, in a down light) REPROOF.
explanation.definitionFit: Material that resists burning and heat damage is described this way.

clue.text: In the French Revolution one might well panic

definitions.text: In the French Revolution one might well
definitions.meaning: literally, be guillotined during the Terror

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to lose composure, while its literal sense recalls guillotine victims of the Terror.

clue.text: Cleaner almost has mug overturned

indicators.note: overturned turns the whole run of almost-has followed by the mug word backwards
almost means the word has loses its final letter

parts.note: a mug is a fool, someone easily duped

explanation.surface: A cleaner nearly has their mug knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: HA (has, 'almost') plus FOOL gives HAFOOL, which 'overturned' turns backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried gourd sponge used for scrubbing in the bath is a cleaning tool.

clue.text: Fruit Roland's peer didn't finish

indicators.note: didn't finish means the name loses its last letter

parts.note: Oliver is Roland's companion among Charlemagne's twelve peers in the Song of Roland

explanation.surface: A fruit is offered to a nobleman who couldn't complete his meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Roland and Oliver are the paired heroes of the medieval French Song of Roland.
explanation.definitionFit: A small oval stone fruit grown around the Mediterranean.

clue.text: A dance enthusiast, chap takes a turn

parts.note: a fan is an enthusiast
Dan is a man's name, standing for any chap
a go is a turn, as in 'your go'

explanation.surface: A keen dancer and his partner take their turn on the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively Spanish dance in triple time, performed by a couple.

clue.text: You could see him there too, but not to the end until now

indicators.note: not to the end means each of the three words stops short of its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone says you could spot him there as well, though not right up to the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not to the end' trims M, E and O off him, there and too, leaving HI, THER and TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal adverb meaning up to this point in time.

clue.text: Include or exclude order from settlement

indicators.note: exclude means the letters for order are taken out of the settlement word

parts.note: a compromise is a settlement reached by both sides giving ground
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A rule-maker asks whether to include or exclude an instruction from a legal settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Include or exclude' looks like a choice of definitions; only 'Include' defines, and 'exclude' removes OM.
explanation.definitionFit: To consist of or contain parts is the sense here.

clue.text: Ring a bird before it's full-grown, they say

indicators.note: they say signals that the bird word is to be heard spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a cygnet is a young swan

explanation.surface: Someone telephones a young bird before it grows up, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a verb meaning call; it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A seal ring engraved with initials or a crest, worn on the finger.

clue.text: The making of a saint, a saint on icon, possibly

indicators.note: possibly means the letters might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A painted holy image depicting a saint marks someone's elevation to sainthood.
explanation.definitionFit: The formal church process declaring a dead person holy, elevating them to sainthood.

clue.text: Capital provided by Eddy, Sally and Kit

indicators.note: capital here is a capital letter, the opening letter that the name Eddy provides

parts.note: a sally is a witty remark, a quip

explanation.surface: Three people, Eddy, Sally and Kit, chip in money for a venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' and 'Kit' look like names alongside Eddy; Sally is a witticism and Kit is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To kit out is to supply with gear, a synonym.

clue.text: Girl comes in on time, as often as not

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: comes in places the girl's name inside the word for time

parts.note: an age is a long period of time
Vera is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl arrives punctually most of the time.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means typically, in the usual run of things.

clue.text: Match gone out? It could be made to fizzle out

indicators.note: could be made to suggests the letters can be worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Has the match died? Perhaps it could be persuaded to splutter out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be made to' rearranges MATCH GONE OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to end in nothing, to fail.

clue.text: In sporting events, that slice is disastrous

indicators.note: a disastrous slice in golf goes badly astray, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: During a sports meeting, a golfer's sliced shot proves calamitous.
explanation.definitionFit: Track and field contests such as running and jumping events.

clue.text: Tripped and fell after beginning to slip

indicators.note: after puts the fall word behind the opening letter in the answer
beginning to takes the opening letter of slip

parts.note: tumbled means fell down

explanation.surface: Someone tripped and fell after starting to slip.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose one's footing and lurch is a synonym for tripping.

clue.text: Some sheets remain — five hundred and fifty-nine, roughly

parts.note: be can mean remain, exist, as in 'let it be'
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: roughly means the following letters are only approximately in order and need rearranging

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An inventory notes that about 559 sheets are left over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' rearranges D, L and NINE into DLINEN, after BE.
explanation.definitionFit: Household textiles such as sheets and pillowcases go by this collective name.

clue.text: When to start shooting almost first bit of the…

parts.note: the Glorious Twelfth, 12 August, opens the British grouse-shooting season
nigh means nearly, almost

indicators.note: first bit of takes the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A clue spilling into the next describes the start of the season leading into a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the 'play' at the start of 21 across, carried on by the dots. The Glorious Twelfth (12 August) is the British grouse-shooting opening day.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Shakespeare comedy, so it is a play.

clue.text: A point in time

definitions.meaning: a full stop, the punctuation point
a span of time, an era

explanation.definitionFit: The word names the dot ending a sentence and also an era or stretch of history.

clue.text: Attacked for being drunk

explanation.definitionFit: The word means pelted with rocks and, in slang, very intoxicated.

clue.text: …play — The Bells, for example

parts.note: The Bells is the Victorian sensation drama that made Henry Irving's name, an example of this sort of play

explanation.surface: A clue continued from the previous one names a famous Victorian stage hit.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bells (1871), starring Henry Irving, is a classic of the sensational, emotionally overblown Victorian stage genre.
explanation.definitionFit: A sensational play with exaggerated emotion and stock characters, a genre typical of Victorian theatre.

clue.text: Girl needs a helper when climbing

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing reads the pieces upwards, so backwards

parts.note: an is the form of a before a vowel
an aid is a helper or assistant

explanation.surface: A girl needs an assistant when she goes mountaineering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' becomes AN; AN AID read upwards ('when climbing') gives the name.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female given name, a girl's name.

clue.text: Leave without trouble

parts.note: ex means without, as in ex dividend
to eat is to trouble or worry, as in 'what's eating you?'

explanation.surface: Someone takes time off without any bother.
explanation.walkthrough: An exeat is leave of absence from a British school or college.
explanation.definitionFit: Permission for temporary absence from school or college, granted as leave.

clue.text: Transport available in April and August only

indicators.note: available in says the vehicle can be found within the words April and August

explanation.surface: A travel service runs only in spring and summer months.
explanation.walkthrough: 'available in' finds it running across the end of April, 'and' and the start of August.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage with a folding hood, a means of conveyance.

clue.text: Girl seeing a lot of soldiers

parts.note: Di is short for Diana, a girl's name
vision is the faculty of seeing

explanation.surface: A girl is dating a whole troop of soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: An army formation of several brigades, a large body of troops.

clue.text: Refusal to involve part of Ulster in a bargain

indicators.note: to involve means the Ulster letters are taken inside the bargain word

parts.note: a deal is a bargain
NI, Northern Ireland, makes up most of the old province of Ulster

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to bring a piece of Northern Ireland into a negotiated agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A refusal to accept or grant something is a synonym.

clue.text: It's unfair, so I'd need to be concerned

indicators.note: concerned means troubled or agitated, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the arrangement is unfair, so they ought to be worried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be concerned' rearranges SO I'D NEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Biased, favouring one party over another, is the sense.
